{{recipesummary|category=Confection recipes|time=45 minutes|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Confections|Confectionery]]

'''Acid drops''' are a hard candy or [[Cookbook:Confections|confection]] made very sour through the addition of acid<ref>https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/acid%20drop</ref>. Citric acid and tartaric acid are commonly used.

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (480 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|mL]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 cup (240 mL) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (2.5 mL) [[Cookbook:Cream of Tartar|cream of tartar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] (15 mL) [[Cookbook:Citric acid|citric acid]] <ref>In the United States, citric acid is available from some Armenian and South Asian grocers, and on-line from cheese-making suppliers.</ref>
* [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|Powdered sugar]]

==Procedure==
#Bring the sugar, water and cream of tartar to boil over medium-low heat. Stir gently until syrup reaches [[Cookbook:Cooking Sugar|310°F (155°C/hard crack stage)]] or is pale brown. Syrup should harden completely when dropped on to a cold plate and snap between the teeth when cold.
# Pour the mixture onto an oiled heatproof work surface, and sprinkle with the citric acid.
#Use a greased [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]] to fold in the sides and thoroughly work the acid in.
#When the candy is cool enough to touch but still pliable, roll it into sticks and snip off drop-sized bits.
#[[Cookbook:Sifter|Sift]] powdered sugar onto the candies, and shake to coat.
#Allow to cool and harden completely. Store in an air-tight container.

==Notes==
